raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Builds on #64980 (W8A16 skinny GEMM for the dense block-FP8 linear layers). At 1-4 tokens the Triton fused MoE on SM90 is far from memory bound: on `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (256 experts, top-8, 128x128 block FP8) the first expert GEMM reads 16 MB of weights in 10.7 us (1.5 TB/s) and the second 8 MB in 5.8 us, and the layer quantizes its activations twice (before each GEMM). Whole expert path per layer at one token, measured in isolation: 27.7 us.

This PR adds a grouped variant of the shape-dynamic W8A16 skinny GEMM for the routed experts: one CTA per (token, expert) pair and output block, BF16 activations, FP8 weights with their 128x128 scales, FP32 accumulation, routing weight folded into the second GEMM's epilogue. `TritonExperts` takes it for 128x128 block-FP8 layers that have a plan for their expert shapes, at the planned token counts (1-4), without EP all2all or LoRA; on that path there is no activation quantization. Above the planned token counts and everywhere else, nothing changes. The layer reports `expects_unquantized_inputs` so that the prepare step hands it BF16 activations; for other token counts it quantizes them itself, with the same kernel as before.

## Claims

- **Expert path per layer, isolated (H200, cold weights, disjoint expert sets):** 1 token 27.7 -> 17.8 us (-36%), 2 tokens 34.0 -> 25.6 us (-25%), 4 tokens 49.6 -> 42.4 us (-15%). 8 tokens measure -8% in isolation but +4% TPOT in the model (see Details), so the plans stop at 4.
- **E2E, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, H200 TP=1, on top of #64980:** median TPOT -10.2% at one request (3.574 -> 3.208 ms), -8.3% at 2, -4.5% at 4, unchanged at 8 (Triton path).
- **E2E, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` (128 experts, plans for 1-2 tokens):** median TPOT -9.9% at one request (4.166 -> 3.755 ms), -6.3% at 2; 4 and 8 requests take the Triton path (a plan for 4 tokens made that model 2% slower, see Details).
- **Accuracy:** W8A16 is closer to the dequantized reference than the W8A8 Triton path (max relative error 3.6e-3 vs 4.0e-2 on random experts); GSM8K 0.7354 / 0.7369 vs 0.7430 for the base (run-to-run spread of this model is 0.728-0.741).
- **Applies to** any 128x128 block-FP8 MoE layer on SM90 whose expert shapes have a plan; this PR ships plans for the Qwen3.5/3.6-35B-A3B experts (`(1024, 2048)` gate_up, `(2048, 512)` down) and the Qwen3-30B-A3B experts (`(1536, 2048)`, `(2048, 768)`). Other shapes keep the Triton path until measured.

## Validation

### Kernel configs

Sweep over block size {32, 64, 128}, outputs per CTA {4, 8, 16, 32}, FP8 vector width {8, 16}, K unroll {1, 2} on H200, CUDA graph replay, 16 rotating expert sets so the weights come from HBM. Best per GEMM and token count (us):

| GEMM | 1 token | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6 gate_up (1024, 2048), 8 pairs/token | 7.30 (bs64, 8 out, vw16) | 11.76 (bs32, 8, vw16) | 21.09 (bs32, 8, vw16) | 37.78 (bs32, 8, vw16) |
| Qwen3.6 down (2048, 512) | 5.58 (bs64, 8, vw8) | 8.67 (bs32, 32, vw8) | 14.24 (bs32, 16, vw16) | 24.38 (bs32, 16, vw16) |
| Qwen3-30B gate_up (1536, 2048) | 9.42 (bs64, 8, vw8) | 16.31 (bs32, 16, vw16) | 29.94 (bs32, 8, vw16) | |
| Qwen3-30B down (2048, 768) | 7.36 (bs32, 8, vw8) | 11.46 (bs32, 16, vw8) | 18.68 (bs32, 8, vw8) | |

Achieved weight bandwidth: 2.3 / 2.9 / 3.2 / 3.55 TB/s for gate_up at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 tokens (the 8 MB down GEMM is latency bound at one token: 1.5 TB/s).

### Expert path, isolated

Same setup, whole routed-expert path of one layer (quantize + GEMM + activation + quantize + GEMM + top-k sum for Triton; GEMM + activation + GEMM + sum here), 256 experts, top-8, `K=2048`, `I=512`:

| tokens | Triton fused MoE (W8A8) | this PR (W8A16) | change | max rel. error vs fp32 reference: Triton / this PR |
|---:|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 27.7 us | 17.8 us | -36% | 4.0e-2 / 3.6e-3 |
| 2 | 34.0 | 25.6 | -25% | 4.7e-2 / 4.2e-3 |
| 4 | 49.6 | 42.4 | -15% | 4.5e-2 / 4.3e-3 |
| 8 | 77.8 | 71.3 | -8% | 5.3e-2 / 4.2e-3 |

Same for the `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` experts (128 experts, top-8, `K=2048`, `I=768`):

| tokens | Triton fused MoE (W8A8) | this PR (W8A16) | change |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 30.3 us | 21.4 us | -29% |
| 2 | 41.2 | 32.4 | -21% |
| 4 | 63.5 | 56.1 | -12% |

### E2E

H200 NVL, TP=1, nightly image with #64980 applied in both arms, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --seed 0`; 32 prompts at concurrency 1, 8x the concurrency otherwise. Four server launches on one GPU in the order PR, base, base, PR. Median TPOT (ms), both runs:

| conc. | without | with this PR | change |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 3.577 / 3.570 | 3.211 / 3.205 | -10.2% |
| 2 | 3.966 / 3.965 | 3.640 / 3.631 | -8.3% |
| 4 | 4.693 / 4.692 | 4.489 / 4.474 | -4.5% |
| 8 | 5.758 / 5.750 | 5.753 / 5.759 | 0 |

The server log shows the warmup: `Warming up CuTeDSL compile_units=19 names=('shape-dynamic block-FP8 skinny MoE GEMM', 'shape-dynamic block-FP8 skinny GEMM')`.

An nsys trace of single-request decode with this PR shows 914 kernels per step (1154 without: the two quantization kernels and the two Triton GEMMs per layer become two grouped GEMMs) and a median step of 3141 us; the 80 grouped GEMMs take 7.3 + 5.7 us per layer as in the isolated measurement.

Same setup, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` (the 4-request row was measured with a 4-token plan that this PR does not ship; the shipped plans stop at 2 tokens, so 4 and 8 requests run the unchanged Triton path):

| conc. | without | with this PR | change |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 4.166 / 4.166 | 3.755 / 3.754 | -9.9% |
| 2 | 4.614 / 4.615 | 4.322 / 4.322 | -6.3% |
| 4 (4-token plan, not shipped) | 5.410 / 5.374 | 5.507 / 5.500 | +2.1% |
| 8 (Triton path) | 6.669 / 6.720 | 6.753 / 6.778 | +1.0% |

### Accuracy

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions): with this PR 0.7354 / 0.7369; without 0.7430 (and 0.7278 / 0.7362 / 0.7407 for the plain nightly image in other runs of the same night).

### Tests

`tests/kernels/test_skinny_fp8_moe_gemm.py` (new): every shipped plan cell, activations per token and per pair, with and without the routing weight, against an fp32 reference on dequantized experts; padded (-1) and out-of-range expert ids produce zero rows; input validation incl. routing-weight dtype; and one expert per pair reproduces the dense W8A16 skinny GEMM. `tests/kernels/moe/test_skinny_fp8_moe.py` (new) drives `FusedMoEKernel` + `TritonExperts` at 1, 2 and 4 tokens on a planned expert shape: the path is taken (both grouped GEMM launches observed), the output matches the dequantized experts, the same kernel object without plans runs the Triton W8A8 path, and an unplanned expert shape never defers the input quantization (4 passed on H200). On H200 (nightly image with #64980 and this branch applied): 42 passed.

## Details

- **Why 4 tokens and not 8.** The kernel reads an expert's weights once per (token, expert) pair; the Triton path groups pairs by expert and reads each expert once. With 8 tokens of real traffic enough pairs share experts that this costs more than the kernel saves: a run with plans up to 8 tokens gave 6.005 / 6.010 ms at 8 requests against 5.764 ms without (+4%), although the isolated measurement with disjoint expert sets was 8% faster. At 4 tokens Qwen3.6 (256 experts) still gains 4.5%, while Qwen3-30B (128 experts, so more sharing) loses 2%, which is why its plans stop at 2 tokens. A per-expert grouping of the pairs (read each expert once, as the Triton path does) would lift both limits and is the natural follow-up.
- **Padded pairs.** vLLM's warmup and profiling runs route padded tokens to expert `-1`; the kernel skips those pairs and writes zero rows, so the top-k sum stays finite.
- **Why `expects_unquantized_inputs`.** The prepare step quantizes activations before `apply`; the kernel needs them in BF16. When the layer has a plan it asks for unquantized activations and quantizes them in `apply` for token counts that take the Triton path, with the same `moe_kernel_quantize_input` call, so those counts see the same kernels as before. DP, EP all2all, LoRA and `expert_map` layers never take the path.
- **Eligibility is decided before the path is taken.** `TritonExperts` checks both expert stacks (contiguity, scale shapes, the configs' divisibility) and the routing weights per call and otherwise runs the Triton path; the kernel wrapper only re-validates. Ids outside `[0, E)` produce zero rows like padding.
- **Two kernels, one loop.** The grouped kernel repeats the dense skinny kernel's tile loop and reduction (about 60 lines) rather than threading an expert index through the dense kernel, so the dense path stays untouched and both can be tuned separately; folding them into one kernel once both have settled is a reasonable follow-up.
- **Workspace.** The grouped kernel writes into the same `workspace2` / `workspace13` buffers the Triton path uses (`(tokens * top_k, N)` and `(tokens * top_k, N / 2)`), so no extra memory.
- **Plans** live next to the dense FP8 plans in `skinny_gemm_plans.py`, keyed by one expert's `(N, K)` and the token count, under capability `(9, 0)`.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""TritonExperts on the grouped W8A16 skinny path for block-FP8 experts."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.moe.utils import (
+    make_dummy_moe_config,
+    make_test_quant_config,
+    modular_triton_fused_moe,
+)
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl import skinny_fp8_moe_gemm
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm_plans import (
+    SKINNY_FP8_MOE_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import fused_topk
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+    pytest.skip("CUDA only", allow_module_level=True)
+if not skinny_fp8_moe_gemm.shape_dynamic_skinny_fp8_moe_gemm.is_available():
+    pytest.skip("cuteDSL is not available", allow_module_level=True)
+_CAPABILITY = current_platform.get_device_capability()
+if _CAPABILITY not in SKINNY_FP8_MOE_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY:
+    pytest.skip(
+        f"no skinny FP8 MoE GEMM plans for {_CAPABILITY}", allow_module_level=True
+    )
+
+# One expert shape with a plan: Qwen3.5/3.6-35B-A3B (gate_up (1024, 2048),
+# down (2048, 512)). Only the per-expert (N, K) matters for the plan.
+E, N, K, TOPK = 16, 512, 2048, 4
+BLOCK = [128, 128]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def setup_cuda():
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
+
+
+def _dequant(w: torch.Tensor, s: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return w.float() * s.repeat_interleave(BLOCK[0], 1).repeat_interleave(BLOCK[1], 2)
+
+
+def _reference(a, w1, w2, w1_s, w2_s, topk_weights, topk_ids):
+    """Dequantized experts in fp32 (the W8A16 path quantizes no activation)."""
+    d1, d2 = _dequant(w1, w1_s), _dequant(w2, w2_s)
+    out = torch.zeros(a.shape[0], K, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for m in range(a.shape[0]):
+        for j in range(TOPK):
+            e = int(topk_ids[m, j])
+            h = a[m].float() @ d1[e].t()
+            h = torch.nn.functional.silu(h[:N]) * h[N:]
+            out[m] += topk_weights[m, j].float() * (h @ d2[e].t())
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("M", [1, 2, 4])

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+from cuda.bindings.driver import CUstream
+from cutlass import const_expr
+
+# Weight quantization block (N and K) of the block-scaled FP8 checkpoints.
+_QUANT_BLOCK = 128
+# A is read in 128-bit vectors of BF16.
+_A_VECTOR = 8
+
+
+class CuteSkinnyFp8BlockGemm:
+    """W8A16 block-scaled FP8 GEMM for small token counts.
+
+    Computes ``C[M, N] = A[M, K] @ (B[N, K] * S)^T`` where ``A`` is BF16, ``B``
+    is FP8 E4M3 and ``S[N / 128, K / 128]`` holds one FP32 scale per 128x128
+    weight block. The activation is not quantized. Accumulation is FP32 and the
+    output is BF16.
+
+    One CTA computes ``outputs_per_block`` outputs (all inside one 128-row
+    scale block); its threads stride over K in ``vector_width``-wide FP8
+    vectors, each of which lies inside one 128-wide scale block, so a thread
+    scales its partial dot product once per vector. Partial sums are reduced
+    per warp and then across warps through shared memory. N and K are runtime
+    values; the tiny M dimension is unrolled.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        num_rows: int,
+        block_size: int,
+        outputs_per_block: int,
+        vector_width: int = 8,
+        k_unroll: int = 1,
+        use_pdl: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        if block_size % cute.arch.WARP_SIZE != 0:
+            raise ValueError("block_size must be a multiple of the warp size")
+        if vector_width not in (8, 16):
+            raise ValueError("vector_width must be 8 or 16")
+        if _QUANT_BLOCK % outputs_per_block != 0:
+            raise ValueError("outputs_per_block must divide the 128-row scale block")
+        self.num_rows = num_rows
+        self.block_size = block_size
+        self.outputs_per_block = outputs_per_block
+        self.vector_width = vector_width
+        self.a_vectors = vector_width // _A_VECTOR
+        self.k_unroll = k_unroll
+        self.use_pdl = use_pdl
+        self.num_warps = block_size // cute.arch.WARP_SIZE
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        gA: cute.Tensor,
+        gB: cute.Tensor,
+        gS: cute.Tensor,
+        gC: cute.Tensor,
+        stream: CUstream,
+    ) -> None:
+        n = cute.size(gB, mode=[0])
+        k = cute.size(gA, mode=[1])
+        copy_a = cute.make_copy_atom(
+            cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(),
+            cutlass.BFloat16,
+            num_bits_per_copy=_A_VECTOR * cutlass.BFloat16.width,
+            load_cache_mode=cute.nvgpu.LoadCacheMode.ALWAYS,
+        )
+        copy_b = cute.make_copy_atom(
+            cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(),
+            cutlass.Float8E4M3FN,
+            num_bits_per_copy=self.vector_width * cutlass.Float8E4M3FN.width,

+from __future__ import annotations

+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+from cuda.bindings.driver import CUstream
+from cutlass import const_expr
+
+# Weight quantization block (N and K) of the block-scaled FP8 checkpoints.
+_QUANT_BLOCK = 128
+# A is read in 128-bit vectors of BF16.
+_A_VECTOR = 8
+
+
+class CuteSkinnyFp8BlockMoeGemm:
+    """Grouped W8A16 block-scaled FP8 GEMM for the routed experts of a MoE
+    layer at small token counts.
+
+    For every (token, expert) pair ``p`` computes
+    ``C[p, :] = A[row(p), :] @ (B[e, :, :] * S[e])^T`` (times the routing
+    weight of the pair when ``mul_routed_weight``), where ``e = ids[p]``,
+    ``A`` is BF16, ``B[E, N, K]`` is FP8 E4M3 and ``S[E, N / 128, K / 128]``
+    holds one FP32 scale per 128x128 weight block. With ``a_per_token`` the
+    activation row is the pair's token (``p // top_k``, first GEMM of the
+    layer); otherwise it is the pair itself (second GEMM). The activation is
+    not quantized. Accumulation is FP32 and the output is BF16. A pair whose
+    expert id is negative (padding) or not below ``E`` gets a zero output row.
+
+    One CTA computes ``outputs_per_block`` outputs of one pair; the grid is
+    ``(N / outputs_per_block, num_pairs)``. Each CTA's threads stride over K in
+    ``vector_width``-wide FP8 vectors, each of which lies inside one 128-wide
+    scale block, so a thread scales its partial dot product once per vector.
+    Partial sums are reduced per warp and then across warps through shared
+    memory. ``N`` must be a multiple of 128 so that an expert's rows start on
+    a scale block.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        block_size: int,
+        outputs_per_block: int,
+        vector_width: int = 8,
+        k_unroll: int = 1,
+        a_per_token: bool = True,
+        mul_routed_weight: bool = False,
+        use_pdl: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        if block_size % cute.arch.WARP_SIZE != 0:
+            raise ValueError("block_size must be a multiple of the warp size")
+        if vector_width not in (8, 16):
+            raise ValueError("vector_width must be 8 or 16")
+        if _QUANT_BLOCK % outputs_per_block != 0:
+            raise ValueError("outputs_per_block must divide the 128-row scale block")
+        self.block_size = block_size
+        self.outputs_per_block = outputs_per_block
+        self.vector_width = vector_width
+        self.a_vectors = vector_width // _A_VECTOR
+        self.k_unroll = k_unroll
+        self.a_per_token = a_per_token
+        self.mul_routed_weight = mul_routed_weight
+        self.use_pdl = use_pdl
+        self.num_warps = block_size // cute.arch.WARP_SIZE
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        gA: cute.Tensor,
+        gB: cute.Tensor,
+        gS: cute.Tensor,
+        gIds: cute.Tensor,
+        gW: cute.Tensor,
+        gC: cute.Tensor,
+        n_per_expert: cutlass.Int32,
+        top_k: cutlass.Int32,
+        num_experts: cutlass.Int32,
+        stream: CUstream,
+    ) -> None:
+        num_pairs = cute.size(gC, mode=[0])
+        k = cute.size(gA, mode=[1])
+        copy_a = cute.make_copy_atom(
+            cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(),
+            cutlass.BFloat16,
+            num_bits_per_copy=_A_VECTOR * cutlass.BFloat16.width,
+            load_cache_mode=cute.nvgpu.LoadCacheMode.ALWAYS,
+        )
+        copy_b = cute.make_copy_atom(
+            cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(),
+            cutlass.Float8E4M3FN,
+            num_bits_per_copy=self.vector_width * cutlass.Float8E4M3FN.width,
+            load_cache_mode=cute.nvgpu.LoadCacheMode.STREAMING,
+        )
+        self.kernel(
+            gA,
+            gB,
+            gS,
+            gIds,
+            gW,
+            gC,
+            n_per_expert,
+            top_k,
+            num_experts,
+            k,
+            copy_a,
+            copy_b,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=[cute.ceil_div(n_per_expert, self.outputs_per_block), num_pairs, 1],
+            block=[self.block_size, 1, 1],
+            smem=self.outputs_per_block * self.num_warps * 4,
+            stream=stream,
+            use_pdl=self.use_pdl,
+            min_blocks_per_mp=1,
+        )
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def kernel(
+        self,
+        gA: cute.Tensor,
+        gB: cute.Tensor,
+        gS: cute.Tensor,
+        gIds: cute.Tensor,
+        gW: cute.Tensor,
+        gC: cute.Tensor,
+        n_per_expert: cutlass.Int32,
+        top_k: cutlass.Int32,
+        num_experts: cutlass.Int32,
+        k_extent: cutlass.Int32,
+        copy_a: cute.CopyAtom,
+        copy_b: cute.CopyAtom,
+    ) -> None:
+        tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+        block_idx, pair, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+        warp_idx = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+
+        outputs_per_block: cutlass.Constexpr = self.outputs_per_block
+        vector_width: cutlass.Constexpr = self.vector_width
+        a_vectors: cutlass.Constexpr = self.a_vectors
+        block_size: cutlass.Constexpr = self.block_size
+        num_warps: cutlass.Constexpr = self.num_warps
+        k_tile_size: cutlass.Constexpr = block_size * vector_width
+        vectors_per_scale: cutlass.Constexpr = _QUANT_BLOCK // vector_width
+
+        acc = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+            cute.make_layout((outputs_per_block,), stride=(1,)), cutlass.Float32
+        )
+        acc.fill(0.0)
+
+        if const_expr(self.use_pdl):
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+
+        expert = gIds[pair]
+        a_row = pair
+        if const_expr(self.a_per_token):
+            a_row = pair // top_k
+        n_local = block_idx * outputs_per_block
+        n_base = expert * n_per_expert + n_local
+        n_scale = n_base // _QUANT_BLOCK
+
+        # ((8, K / 8)) for the A row and (E * N, (vector_width, K / vector_width))
+        # for B.
+        gA_vec = cute.logical_divide(gA, (None, _A_VECTOR))
+        gB_vec = cute.logical_divide(gB, (None, vector_width))
+        a_regs = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+            cute.make_layout((a_vectors, _A_VECTOR), stride=(_A_VECTOR, 1)),
+            cutlass.BFloat16,
+        )
+        b_regs = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+            cute.make_layout(
+                (outputs_per_block, vector_width), stride=(vector_width, 1)
+            ),
+            cutlass.Float8E4M3FN,
+        )
+
+        # A negative expert id marks a pair with no expert (padding in warmup
+        # and profiling runs); it and any id outside the stack give a zero row.
+        valid = (expert >= 0) & (expert < num_experts)
+        if valid:
+            num_k_tiles = k_extent // k_tile_size
+            for k_tile in cutlass.range(num_k_tiles, unroll=self.k_unroll):
+                vec_idx = k_tile * block_size + tidx
+                for ni in cutlass.range_constexpr(outputs_per_block):
+                    cute.copy(
+                        copy_b,
+                        gB_vec[n_base + ni, (None, vec_idx)],
+                        b_regs[ni, None],
+                    )
+                for ai in cutlass.range_constexpr(a_vectors):
+                    cute.copy(
+                        copy_a,
+                        gA_vec[a_row, (None, vec_idx * a_vectors + ai)],
+                        a_regs[ai, None],
+                    )
+                scale = gS[n_scale, vec_idx // vectors_per_scale]
+                b_f32 = b_regs.load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+                a_f32 = a_regs.load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+                for ni in cutlass.range_constexpr(outputs_per_block):
+                    part = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+                    for vi in cutlass.range_constexpr(vector_width):
+                        part = (
+                            part
+                            + a_f32[vi // _A_VECTOR, vi % _A_VECTOR] * b_f32[ni, vi]
+                        )
+                    acc[ni] = acc[ni] + part * scale
+
+        for ni in cutlass.range_constexpr(outputs_per_block):
+            acc[ni] = cute.arch.warp_reduction_sum(acc[ni])
+
+        smem = cutlass.utils.SmemAllocator()
+        partials = smem.allocate_tensor(
+            cutlass.Float32,
+            cute.make_layout((outputs_per_block, num_warps), stride=(num_warps, 1)),
+            byte_alignment=16,
+        )
+        with cute.arch.elect_one():
+            for ni in cutlass.range_constexpr(outputs_per_block):
+                partials[ni, warp_idx] = acc[ni]
+
+        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+        if tidx == 0:
+            routed_weight = cutlass.Float32(1.0)
+            # Compile-time and runtime conditions cannot share one `if`.
+            if const_expr(self.mul_routed_weight):  # noqa: SIM102
+                if valid:
+                    routed_weight = gW[pair]
+            for ni in cutlass.range_constexpr(outputs_per_block):
+                total = (
+                    partials[ni, None]
+                    .load()
+                    .reduce(
+                        cute.ReductionOp.ADD,
+                        init_val=cutlass.Float32(0.0),
+                        reduction_profile=0,
+                    )
+                )
+                gC[pair, n_local + ni] = (cutlass.Float32(total) * routed_weight).to(
+                    cutlass.BFloat16
+                )
+
+        if const_expr(self.use_pdl):
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()

+from __future__ import annotations

+

+

+)
+
+QUANT_BLOCK = 128
+# A is read in 128-bit vectors of BF16; B in 64- or 128-bit vectors of FP8.
+_A_VECTOR = 8
+_B_VECTOR_WIDTHS = (8, 16)
+
+
+def can_use_skinny_fp8_gemm(
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    config: SkinnyGemmConfig,
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``a @ dequant(weight, weight_scale).T`` fits ``config``.
+
+    ``weight`` must be a row-major (N, K) FP8 E4M3 tensor and ``weight_scale``
+    a row-major FP32 (ceil(N / 128), K / 128) tensor, the layout the SM90
+    block-FP8 linear kernels keep after loading. ``config.static_k`` is not
+    supported by this kernel.
+    """
+    if a.dim() != 2 or weight.dim() != 2 or weight_scale.dim() != 2:
+        return False
+    m, k = a.shape
+    n = weight.shape[0]
+    scale_shape = ((n + QUANT_BLOCK - 1) // QUANT_BLOCK, k // QUANT_BLOCK)
+    return (
+        m == config.num_rows
+        and config.static_k is None
+        and config.vector_width in _B_VECTOR_WIDTHS
+        and a.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        and weight_scale.dtype == torch.float32
+        and weight.shape[1] == k
+        and weight.is_contiguous()
+        and weight_scale.is_contiguous()
+        and tuple(weight_scale.shape) == scale_shape
+        and n % config.outputs_per_block == 0
+        and k % (config.block_size * config.vector_width) == 0
+        and a_rows_aligned(a, _A_VECTOR)
+    )
+
+
+class ShapeDynamicSkinnyFp8Gemm(CuteDslGemm):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._warmup_configs: set[SkinnyGemmConfig] = set()
+
+    def _compile(self, config: SkinnyGemmConfig) -> None:
+        if config in self._compiled:
+            return
+        import cutlass
+        import cutlass.cute as cute
+        from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor
+
+        from ._skinny_fp8_gemm import CuteSkinnyFp8BlockGemm
+
+        n = cute.sym_int(divisibility=config.outputs_per_block)
+        k = cute.sym_int(divisibility=config.block_size * config.vector_width)
+        n_scale = cute.sym_int()
+        k_scale = cute.sym_int()
+        a = make_fake_tensor(cutlass.BFloat16, (config.num_rows, k), divisibility=8)
+        b = make_fake_tensor(
+            cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, (n, k), divisibility=config.vector_width
+        )
+        s = make_fake_tensor(cutlass.Float32, (n_scale, k_scale), divisibility=1)
+        c = make_fake_tensor(cutlass.BFloat16, (config.num_rows, n), divisibility=1)
+        kernel = CuteSkinnyFp8BlockGemm(
+            num_rows=config.num_rows,
+            block_size=config.block_size,
+            outputs_per_block=config.outputs_per_block,
+            vector_width=config.vector_width,
+            k_unroll=config.k_unroll,
+            use_pdl=self._use_pdl(),
+        )
+        self._compiled[config] = cute.compile(
+            kernel,
+            a,
+            b,
+            s,
+            c,
+            self._stream(),
+            options="--enable-tvm-ffi --ptxas-options -maxrregcount=64",
+        )
+
+    def request_warmup_configs(self, configs: Iterable[SkinnyGemmConfig]) -> None:
+        """Request compilation of measured configs before CUDA graph capture."""
+        self._warmup_configs.update(configs)
+        self._register_warmup_provider()
+
+    def get_cutedsl_warmup_compile_units(self):
+        from vllm.model_executor.warmup.cutedsl_warmup import CuTeDSLCompileUnit
+
+        return tuple(
+            CuTeDSLCompileUnit(
+                name="shape-dynamic block-FP8 skinny GEMM",
+                key=("shape-dynamic-skinny-fp8-gemm", config),
+                compile=partial(self._compile, config),
+            )
+            for config in sorted(
+                self._warmup_configs,
+                key=lambda c: (
+                    c.num_rows,
+                    c.block_size,
+                    c.outputs_per_block,
+                    c.k_unroll,
+                    c.vector_width,
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        a: torch.Tensor,
+        weight: torch.Tensor,
+        weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+        config: SkinnyGemmConfig,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if not can_use_skinny_fp8_gemm(a, weight, weight_scale, config):
+            raise ValueError("inputs do not fit the skinny FP8 GEMM config")
+        self._compile(config)
+        output = torch.empty(
+            (a.shape[0], weight.shape[0]), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=a.device
+        )
+        self._compiled[config](a, weight, weight_scale, output, self._stream())
+        return output
+
